correctness.rationale: Direct zero-sum decomposition Q_p = radial m s^2 F_{m,t}(p) minus a repeated 2x2 fluctuation form is checked algebraically against actual RESULT.md. Concavity of x^(p/2) for 0<p<2 makes fluctuation determinant strictly positive. F(1)=-2t<0 and F(2)=2(m-2)t^2>0; Li–Weston strict-downward propagation excludes multiple nonstrict endpoints and any later p-negative type. The one-dimensional endpoint radial null, Schoenberg Gram ranks and m/t monotonicity follow. The three t->0, t->infinity, m->infinity formulas arise from uniform finite-difference expansions of G_p(1/t), including h(u)>0. Independent direct distance-Q evaluations versus decomposition at several m,t,p gave maximum discrepancy 5.68e-14 and m=3,t=1 root log(2)/log(1.5)=1.7095112913519. Those finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: A weighted corona of a complete graph is a natural nontrivial graph metric family; exact p-negative type controls Hilbert snowflake embeddability and critical embedding rank. Sharp singular edge-length scaling and monotonicity quantify geometry not present in unweighted p=1 QEC tables. The exact threshold and its one-dimensional obstruction are useful benchmarks for rooted graph products, without claiming arbitrary graph universality.

limitations: An unindexed exact generalized-roundness calculation for the weighted complete corona could supersede priority.
The t=0 quotient is equilateral and not part of the positive-length 2m-vertex theorem; limits must not be read as continuity at t=0.
All five original source packages remain unchanged; no GitHub writes, independent peer attestation, or publication.
Supporting finite numerical/exact tests corroborate specific computations but do not establish whole-parameter/infinite statements.
